title: Bhikkhus, if one were to speak rightly about Sāriputta, one could say: 'Sāriputta is the legitimate son of the Blessed One, born of his mouth,…
content: Bhikkhus, if one were to speak rightly about Sāriputta, one could say: 'Sāriputta is the legitimate son of the Blessed One, born of his mouth, born of the Dhamma, fashioned by the Dhamma, an heir of the Dhamma, not an heir of material things.'

title: Reflecting wisely, he uses lodging only to ward off cold, to ward off heat, to ward off the touch of flies, mosquitoes, wind, sun, and…
content:
Reflecting wisely, he uses lodging only to ward off cold, to ward off heat, to ward off the touch of flies, mosquitoes, wind, sun, and creeping things, only to remove the dangers of climate, and only for the purpose of seclusion and quietude.
Reflecting wisely, he uses medicines and medical requisites only to ward off arisen painful feelings and for the sake of complete freedom from affliction.
Bhikkhus, if he did not use thus, harmful, afflicting taints might arise; but when he uses thus, those harmful, afflicting taints do not arise. These, bhikkhus, are called taints that are to be abandoned by using.

title: 'One who clings, bhikkhu, is bound by Māra. One who does not cling is freed from the Evil One.' - 'Venerable Sir, I understand. Well-Gone…
content: 'One who clings, bhikkhu, is bound by Māra. One who does not cling is freed from the Evil One.' - 'Venerable Sir, I understand. Well-Gone Sir, I understand.' - 'How, bhikkhu, do you understand in detail the meaning of my brief statement?' - 'Venerable Sir, one who clings to form is bound by Māra. One who does not cling is freed from the Evil One. One who clings to feeling ... to perception ... to formations ... to consciousness is bound by Māra. One who does not cling is freed from the Evil One. Venerable Sir, this is how I understand in detail the meaning of the Blessed One's brief statement.' - 'Good, good, bhikkhu! It is good that you understand thus the meaning of my brief statement. One who clings to form, bhikkhu, is bound by Māra. One who does not cling is freed from the Evil One. One who clings to feeling ... to perception ... to formations ... to consciousness is bound by Māra. One who does not cling is freed from the Evil One.'

title: And, bhikkhus, how is mindfulness of breathing developed and cultivated so as to perfect the four foundations of mindfulness? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu goes to…
content: And, bhikkhus, how is mindfulness of breathing developed and cultivated so as to perfect the four foundations of mindfulness? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu goes to the forest, to the root of a tree, or to an empty hut, sits down, folding his legs crosswise, keeping his body straight, and establishing mindfulness in front of him. Mindfully he breathes in, mindfully he breathes out ... 'Contemplating relinquishment, I will breathe in,' he trains; 'Contemplating relinquishment, I will breathe out,' he trains. Whenever, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu breathing in long understands: 'I breathe in long'; or breathing out long, he understands: 'I breathe out long' ... breathing in short, he understands: 'I breathe in short'; breathing out short, he understands: 'I breathe out short' ... 'Experiencing the whole body, I will breathe in,' he trains ... 'Tranquilizing the bodily formation, I will breathe in,' he trains; 'Tranquilizing the bodily formation, I will breathe out,' he trains. At that time, bhikkhus, dwelling contemplating the body as a body, a bhikkhu abides ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world. Why is that? Bhikkhus, I say that this is a certain body, namely, in-breath and out-breath. Therefore, bhikkhus, at that time, dwelling contemplating the body as a body, a bhikkhu abides ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world.

title: Just as, sisters, a skilled butcher or his apprentice, after killing a cow, cuts it up with a sharp butcher's knife without damaging the inner…
content: Just as, sisters, a skilled butcher or his apprentice, after killing a cow, cuts it up with a sharp butcher's knife without damaging the inner flesh or the outer skin, and then cuts, severs, and removes all the inner sinews, inner tendons, and inner ligaments. After cutting, severing, and removing them, and after removing the outer skin, he covers the cow again with that same skin and says: 'This cow is attached to this skin as before' — would that person be speaking correctly?" "No, venerable sir." "Why is that?" "Even though, venerable sir, that skilled butcher or his apprentice, after killing the cow ... covers it again with that same skin, he could say: 'This cow is attached to this skin as before' — but the cow is already separated from that skin." "I give this simile, sisters, to convey the meaning. The meaning here is this: 'Inner flesh' is a synonym for the six internal bases. 'Outer skin' is a synonym for the six external bases. 'Inner sinews, inner tendons, inner ligaments' are a synonym for desire and lust and greed. 'The sharp butcher's knife' is a synonym for noble wisdom. With that noble wisdom, he cuts, severs, and removes the inner defilements, inner fetters, inner bonds.

title: Bhikkhus, with these words, the mind of the Blessed One Vipassī, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, inclined towards inaction, to passivity, not wishing to…
content: Bhikkhus, with these words, the mind of the Blessed One Vipassī, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, inclined towards inaction, to passivity, not wishing to teach the Dhamma. Then a certain Great Brahmā, having known with his mind the thought of the Blessed One Vipassī, thought: 'Alas, the world will be destroyed, the world will perish, if the mind of the Blessed One Vipassī, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, inclines towards inaction, to passivity, not wishing to teach the Dhamma!' Bhikkhus, that Great Brahmā, just as a strong man might stretch his bent arm or bend his outstretched arm, vanished from the Brahmā world and appeared before the Blessed One Vipassī, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One. Bhikkhus, then the Great Brahmā arranged his upper robe on one shoulder, knelt on his right knee on the ground, saluted the Blessed One Vipassī with joined palms, and said: 'Venerable Sir, let the Blessed One teach the Dhamma! Let the Well-Gone teach the Dhamma! There are beings with little dust in their eyes who will be lost if they do not hear the Dhamma. Having heard, they will understand the Dhamma.'

title: Possessing these five qualities, bhikkhus, an elder bhikkhu is loved, liked, respected, and an example for his fellow celibates. What five? He is virtuous, living…
content:
Possessing these five qualities, bhikkhus, an elder bhikkhu is loved, liked, respected, and an example for his fellow celibates. What five? He is virtuous, living restrained by the restraint of the Pātimokkha, perfect in conduct and resort, seeing danger in the slightest faults, undertaking and training in the training rules; he is learned, remembers what he has learned, accumulates what he has learned. Those teachings that are beautiful in the beginning, beautiful in the middle, beautiful in the end, with meaning and phrasing, revealing the completely perfected and purified holy life — such teachings he has learned much, memorized, remembered by repeated recitation, investigated with the mind, and well penetrated by right view; he speaks well, uses fine speech, his words are refined, clear in meaning, his voice not faltering or hoarse, he explains the meaning clearly; he attains without difficulty, without trouble, without effort the four jhānas that are higher states of mind, pleasant abidings in this very life; by the destruction of the taints, he in this very life, with direct knowledge, realizes, attains, and abides in the taintless liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom.
Possessing these five qualities, bhikkhus, an elder bhikkhu is loved, liked, respected, and an example for his fellow celibates.

title: Bhikkhus, for a bhikkhu, those taints that are to be abandoned by seeing have been abandoned by seeing, those taints that are to be abandoned…
content: Bhikkhus, for a bhikkhu, those taints that are to be abandoned by seeing have been abandoned by seeing, those taints that are to be abandoned by restraining have been abandoned by restraining ... That bhikkhu is called one who dwells restraining all taints, who has cut off craving, who has turned away from the fetters, who has fully broken through conceit, who has put an end to suffering.

title: Bhikkhus, when the community of bhikkhus gathers in harmony, disperses in harmony, and carries out Saṅgha business in harmony, then, bhikkhus, the community of bhikkhus…
content: Bhikkhus, when the community of bhikkhus gathers in harmony, disperses in harmony, and carries out Saṅgha business in harmony, then, bhikkhus, the community of bhikkhus will grow and not decline. Bhikkhus, when the community of bhikkhus does not decree what has not been decreed, does not abolish what has been decreed, and lives following the training rules as decreed, then, bhikkhus, the community of bhikkhus will grow and not decline. Bhikkhus, when the community of bhikkhus honors, respects, reveres, and makes offerings to the elder bhikkhus — those of long experience, long ordained, the fathers and leaders of the Saṅgha — and listens to their guidance, then, bhikkhus, the community of bhikkhus will grow and not decline.

title: Elder Soṇa Koḷivisa: Formerly, high in the state, serving the king of Aṅga, Now high in the Dhamma, Soṇa has overcome suffering. Five are cut,…
content:
Elder Soṇa Koḷivisa:

Formerly, high in the state, serving the king of Aṅga,
Now high in the Dhamma, Soṇa has overcome suffering.

Five are cut, five abandoned, five higher qualities are developed.
A bhikkhu who has crossed five strands is called one who has crossed the flood.

A bhikkhu of arrogant nature, heedless, delighting in external tastes,
Does not perfect virtue, concentration, and wisdom.

What should be done is abandoned; what should not be done is done.
For the arrogant and heedless, the taints increase.

Those who are diligently, constantly developing mindfulness of the body,
Do not do what should not be done, persist in what should be done.
For the mindful and aware, the taints are destroyed.

The straight path is taught — walk on it, do not turn back.
Reproach yourself, bring Nibbāna near.

When I was striving with overstrained energy,
The Unsurpassed Teacher of the world,
Using the simile of the lute, the One with the Dhamma-eye, the Seer,
Taught me the Dhamma.

I heard his teaching and dwelled happily in that instruction.
Calm, I practiced to attain the supreme goal.
I have attained the three knowledges; done is the Buddha's teaching.

One who is intent on renunciation, mind inclined to seclusion,
One who is intent on non-hatred, destroying all grasping,

One who is intent on the destruction of craving, mind without delusion,
Seeing the arising of the base, the mind is well liberated.

A bhikkhu whose mind is pure, rightly liberated,
Has nothing stored up, nothing left to do.

Like a solid rock, not shaken by the wind,
So too, regarding all forms, tastes, sounds, scents, touches,

Pleasant and unpleasant phenomena — unshaken,
That one's mind is established, unattached,
Contemplating their destruction.
